historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 company guidance (+0.6%) rising to ~2-2.5% mid-path: price revisions and overseas growth against flat-to-declining domestic volumes. Equity 5yr CAGR 3.68% is the cross-check; the revenue 5yr CAGR (4.95%) is inflated by the FY2022-24 wheat-price pass-through and the FY2020 Allied Pinnacle consolidation, neither of which recurs.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.7% vs revenue 5yr 5.0% and EPS 5yr 12.1%: the EPS figure runs from a FY2021 base (63.95) to an impairment-depressed FY2026 (113.33) that still contains JPY10.7bn of cross-shareholding sale gains; neither end is a clean operating year. Equity growth is muted by JPY32bn of buybacks in FY2025-26 and the JPY14.1bn FY2023 net loss (Allied Pinnacle impairment). None of the three is a reliable forward growth proxy on its own.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; SBC nil throughout): FY2021 31,988 -> FY2026 26,791 (-3.5%/yr) because capex doubled from 2.6% to 4.8% of revenue over the period; the 3yr figure (+81%) runs from the FY2023 trough (4,505, a wheat-price working-capital drain) and is meaningless as a trend. EPS 3yr CAGR is undefined: FY2023 EPS was -34.91 (Allied Pinnacle impairment). Pre-FY2027 EPS and share counts are restated by the parser for three 1.1-for-1 splits.

scenario_narratives.base: Nisshin remains the leader of a four-firm 80%-share domestic flour oligopoly whose input price is set by the government, and uses that cash engine to fund a slow pivot overseas. FY2027 lands on guidance (sales +0.6%, OP JPY46.0bn after the JPY1.5bn Middle-East cost lag), then the Mizushima plant's unit-cost savings, the India yeast business returning to profit as management guided, and cost pass-through catching up lift the EBITDA margin 0.1pp a year to 9.0% by FY2031 -- an OP margin of ~5.7%, a shade above the FY2024 peak and well short of the abandoned MTP 6%. Revenue grows 2-2.5% a year, almost entirely price/mix and North America, against flat-to-falling domestic volume. Capex normalises from the FY2027 peak of JPY48bn to ~1.1x D&A by FY2033. The 16x terminal cap binds, so the value is anchored to a mature-staple multiple, not to the Gordon formula. The cross-shareholding portfolio (JPY150bn listed, JPY110bn after tax) is valued separately in the bridge and its sell-down funds the dividend-plus-buyback programme that owner FCF alone cannot.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'Nisshin Innovation' reset under President Nagaki -- a former Miller Milling head with a majority-outside-director board behind him -- actually changes the earnings model: a second North-American capacity wave, Australia resolved by Plan C (sale or concentration), India yeast back to 4-7% market growth with positive margins, and portfolio pruning in Others. The EBITDA margin reaches 10.3% (OP ~7%) by FY2032, revenue compounds 3-3.5% on price revisions plus overseas and the Nomura frozen-food plant, and the market pays a mature-compounder 18x FCF at exit with 1.5% terminal growth. Buybacks and the JPY40bn+ cross-shareholding unwind continue to shrink the count, which this model treats as value-neutral but which supports the multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes are cost pass-through lag, the two chronic problem subsidiaries, and Japanese demographics. Middle-East-driven energy, packaging and freight inflation keeps running ahead of the government wheat price and the June 2026 flour price revision, India yeast misses its FY2027 recovery and needs a second impairment, Australia requires exit costs rather than a turnaround, and the new leadership spends its first MTP cycle restructuring rather than growing. EBITDA slides to 7.8% (OP ~4.5%, the FY2021-22 level), revenue barely grows (0.5-1%) as domestic volume decline offsets pricing, capex stays elevated at 4.5% of sales because the plant consolidation programme cannot be stopped mid-way, and the exit multiple compresses to 14x with 0.5% terminal growth. There is no solvency axis: net debt ex-leases is negative and the securities portfolio alone covers all borrowings three times over, so the bear case is a value trap, not a distress case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A defensive, low-growth staple valued as the sum of (i) an operating flour-and-food business discounted at a JPY-built 6% WACC with the terminal value capped at a mature-staple 16x owner FCF, and (ii) a JPY180bn investment-securities portfolio taken separately at fair value net of the tax the sell-down programme will crystallise, less NCI and the unfunded pension. Risk is charged once -- in the three driver paths and their 25/50/25 weights -- not again in the discount rate. The FY2026 net-income trough (India impairment) is not extrapolated: the flows start from operating profit, which the impairment did not touch, and the FY2027 recovery management guided is what the Y1-Y5 margin path follows. House and street bases coincide because SBC is nil.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal cap: at 6.0% WACC and 1.0% g the Gordon multiple is 20x; the 16x cap binds and sets ~60% of EV. Each 1x of cap is worth roughly JPY80/share.
WACC: a 0.5-0.6 beta would justify ~5% and add several hundred yen per share; the 6% rate is a deliberate conservatism on a stock with ~80% of value in the terminal.

Cross-shareholding portfolio: JPY110bn net of tax (~JPY395/share) marked at 30 Jun 2026 fair value; a 20% Japanese equity drawdown removes ~JPY80/share, and the deferred-tax haircut could be argued away (+JPY145/share) if holdings are never sold.

Capex normalisation: the base assumes capex falls from 6.0% to 4.2% of sales by FY2033; if management keeps spending 5%+ (second NA wave, further plant consolidation) with no margin payoff, mature FCF is a third lower.
Lease current-portion and current long-term-debt splits at 30 Jun 2026 are estimated from the FY2026 yuho (JPY~5bn combined, ~JPY18/share); refresh from the H1 FY2027 balance sheet when filed.
Working-capital capture at -18% of revenue growth is calibrated to a 19.5%-of-sales NWC base; a wheat-price spike (FY2023 drained JPY20bn) would hit interim FCF harder than the smooth path implies.

inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: the only share-based pay is a directors' stock-remuneration trust (FY2026 yuho, 'Stock-based remuneration plan', 56,000 shares held by Master Trust Bank), well under 0.05% of revenue; no cash-flow add-back line exists. Kept explicit at 0% per the SBC-zero rule.
inputs.share_count_basis: 282,111,891 issued less 2,497,549 treasury shares at 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin) = 279,614,342. No convertibles or options disclosed; the 56,000 trust shares are immaterial. Held FLAT: SBC is nil and buybacks (JPY14.1bn FY2025, JPY17.9bn FY2026, JPY20bn authorised Oct-2025) are value-neutral in this model -- they fund the flat count, and the count already reflects the FY2026 cancellation of 8.5m shares.
inputs.net_debt_note: At 30 Jun 2026: short-term borrowings 12,431 + bonds 20,000 + long-term borrowings 10,999 + current portion of long-term borrowings ~846 (FY2026 fair-value note: 12,031 incl. current vs 11,185 non-current; Q1 split not disclosed, March figure carried) = 44,276 borrowings; plus lease liabilities 46,356 non-current + ~4,258 estimated current portion (one year of repayments, sits in 'other current liabilities') = 50,614; total_debt 94,890. Cash and deposits 84,952 (JPY2.4bn of government bonds in current 'Securities' omitted, ~JPY9/share). Net debt 9,938. Ex-leases the group is net cash JPY40.7bn, >1x the FCF base, so interest income is stripped.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the flows' own currency. 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + beta 0.8 x Japan ERP 5.75% = cost of equity ~6.3% (observed beta for this defensive staple is 0.3-0.5; 0.8 is a deliberate margin). After-tax cost of debt ~2.5% blended across ~1% yen borrowings/bonds and 5-7% overseas lease liabilities. Debt ~14% of EV-weight -> WACC 6.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the flows and the probability weights, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. The J-GAAP parent expenses operating leases; overseas subsidiaries (Miller Milling, Allied Pinnacle, SE Asia) book IFRS16/ASC842 right-of-use assets, which is why the lease liability KPI jumped from JPY760m to JPY31.0bn in FY2020. Lease liabilities (JPY50.6bn incl. estimated current portion) sit in total_debt; lease principal repayments (JPY4,258m FY2026, 0.49% of revenue) are NOT deducted from the flows but the equivalent lease-asset renewal is charged inside capex_pct_path (+0.5pp every year); lease interest stays in financing (WACC). EBITDA is therefore post-IFRS16 for the overseas subs and D&A includes right-of-use depreciation, which is consistent with the liability sitting in debt. Sanity multiples must use the lease-inclusive EV against the post-IFRS16 EBITDA of JPY74.5bn (OP 46,685 + depreciation 26,568 + goodwill amortisation 1,268).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests JPY19,995m at 30 Jun 2026 deducted at book (equity_bridge). The flows are therefore 100%-consolidated operating profit; NCI's FY2026 profit share was JPY1,346m (4.0% of profit), so book (~15x that share) is a fair deduction. Calibration: FY2026 EBIT 46,685 x (1-0.31) = 32,213 vs reported profit 33,935 less ~1.9bn of net non-operating/extraordinary items after tax -- ties within noise.
inputs.matching_asset_note: Every income stream outside operating profit is excluded from the flows, and its asset is in the bridge: interest income 1,229 (cash), dividend income 3,599 and gains on sale of investment securities 10,730 (listed cross-shareholdings, bridge at fair value net of tax), equity-method profit 2,229 (affiliates at carrying value), rental income 286 (ignored, no asset). Cross-shareholding sale proceeds (JPY12.6bn FY2026; JPY40bn+ programme FY2025-29) are therefore NOT in the FCF -- they are the bridge asset being monetised, which is also why total shareholder returns (dividends 17.4bn + buybacks 17.9bn in FY2026) exceed owner FCF without the model being wrong.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' -- a JPY-reporting staple-food industrial with IFRS16 leases at overseas subs, a 2-4% NCI and a large cross-shareholding portfolio, so owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections a1, b, c, d, e and f all apply). Not a bank/REIT/holdco; first valuation of this ticker, no prior model to match. FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 31 Mar 2026); Y1 = FY2027, 10-year explicit horizon because capex is still normalising from the Mizushima/Nomura/North-America cycle and the FCF margin is not mature until ~Y5. The FY2026 base year is treated as an impairment-depressed ONE-OFF for net income (JPY8.7bn India yeast impairment + JPY2.0bn factory-closure loss, both below operating profit), but it is NOT a depressed base for the flows: the component build starts from operating profit (46,685, +0.7% YoY) and EBITDA, which the impairment did not touch, so there is no double penalty and no extrapolation of the impairment-year profit. FY2027 Y1 is anchored to company guidance (sales 870.0bn +0.6%, OP 46.0bn incl. a JPY1.5bn Middle-East cost lag, capex 48.0bn) and management's guided India recovery and Mizushima savings are what drive the Y2-Y5 margin path. Buybacks are real (repurchaser), so the flat count is funded. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide and band_position is null by construction. Price is a regular-session intraday print, not after-hours.

bear.note: EBITDA 7.8% = ~4.5% OP margin, back to FY2021-22 levels (4.3-4.6%) as cost lags persist, India yeast misses its FY2027 recovery and Australia needs a Plan D; capex stays above the D&A replacement level because the group keeps building through the downturn.

base.growth_note: Y1 = FY2027 guidance 870.0bn (+0.6%); Q1 FY2027 ran +1.1%. Y2-Y5 2-2.5% = ~1.5-2pt price/mix (June 2026 flour price revision, inflation pass-through) + ~1pt overseas (North America capacity, Vietnam B2C, Nomura frozen-food plant from mid-2027) against -0.5pt domestic volume from demographics. Fades to 1.5% by Y9-10.
base.margin_note: FY2026 EBITDA margin 8.61% (OP 5.40% + D&A 3.22%); FY2027 guidance implies ~8.65% (OP 46.0bn = 5.29% after the JPY1.5bn Middle-East cost lag, D&A rising ~10% on the Mizushima step-up). Y2-Y5 +0.1pp/yr to 9.0% from Mizushima unit-cost savings post Okayama/Sakaide closures, India yeast returning to profit (guided FY2027), Australia Plan C, and cost pass-through catching up. 9.0% EBITDA = ~5.7% OP margin, just above the FY2024 peak (5.6%) and below the original MTP 6.0% target that management has already abandoned.
base.capex_note: FY2027 guided capex 48.0bn = 5.5% of sales + 0.5pp lease-asset renewal (treatment A) = 6.0%. Normalises to 4.2% (3.7% capex, ~1.1x D&A, + 0.5pp leases) by Y7 as the Mizushima / Nomura / North-America cycle completes. FY2021-23 ran 2.3-2.7% but that under-invested; FY2025-26 ran 4.8-4.9%.
base.tax_note: Statutory 30.6%; actual effective 32.6% (FY2025) and 33.7% (FY2026, non-deductible impairment). 31.0% flat on operating EBIT; cash taxes paid 16,046 in FY2026 vs current tax 18,178.
base.wc_note: Receivables 113.1bn + inventories 128.1bn - trade payables 72.0bn = 169bn net working capital = 19.5% of revenue; growth consumes cash at ~18% of the revenue increase. Negative capture per the manufacturer rule.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 6.0%/1.0% is 20.2x FCF; the 16x cap binds, deliberately, for a structurally slow domestic staple (own history ~15-20x P/E, EV/EBITDA 6-8x). Terminal growth 1.0% in JPY: ~2% nominal overseas and price inflation on 30% of sales against a shrinking Japanese population on 70%.

bull.note: EBITDA 10.3% = ~7.0% OP margin, i.e. Nisshin Innovation delivers the original MTP 6% OP margin and then some; capex stays a touch higher to fund a second North-American expansion wave.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: the final-year MTP targets were cut mid-plan (OP JPY57bn -> 46bn), FY2027 OP is guided down again, and two subsidiaries (Australia, India yeast) have absorbed years of restructuring and an JPY8.7bn impairment without resolution -- a pattern, not a one-off -- although there is no solvency or covenant risk. Bull down to 25%: it needs North America, Australia, India AND a new-CEO strategic reset to all deliver simultaneously, plus a re-rating to 18x FCF for a business that has never grown faster than wheat-price inflation. Base at 50% is management's own guided path with the margin recovery they have already described.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
